question: What does STOPPED actually emit? (slate, or nothing?)
test: STOP the channel, then run an 8s ffmpeg capture on the caption loopback
result: The probe TIMED OUT after 60s with NO stream and produced no file. Channel state: STOPPED, source=-, pid=-.
conclusion: STOPPED emits NO MEDIA AT ALL. It does not generate slate on this output. Therefore a STOP cannot be used as a slate->program visual anchor.
implication: The anchor must come from the ON_AIR transition itself: media APPEARS at the moment the channel starts. The capture must already be running so the first emitted media IS the transition.
design: Start capture while STOPPED (receiving nothing), issue START at a logged wall time, and treat THE FIRST MEDIA SAMPLE in the capture as the program-onset anchor. That is an observable content onset, not an inferred offset.
